# The Hive's rules

> **Laboratory.** The Hive's rule language exists to press on the language
> and to drive Quantum OS; it carries no stability promise and may change in
> any release (`SUPPORT_TIERS.md`).

A `q:application type="hive"` is the rules of the Hive, the set of daemons
that watch a Quantum OS system (`os/` in the repository): what the Hive
offers when something happens, and what its actuator may do at all, in
tags. It compiles to two files the daemons load: `rules.toml`, which
`hive-synapse` reads to turn an event into offers an administrator may
approve, and `whitelist.toml`, which `hive-actuator` checks every action
against before running it. There is nothing to compute in a hive: no
statements, no expressions, and text where a tag goes is a compile error.

```bash
quantum run hive.q --out projects/hive/hive   # writes rules.toml and whitelist.toml
python scripts/generate-hive-config.py        # the OS's own: os/config/hive/hive.q -> os/config/hive/
```

Two things are checked before anything runs. A `{field}` in an offer is a
field the event has, of the right type, and it is filled in by
`hive-synapse` from the event itself, never from the model's text. And an
offer the file's own whitelist would refuse does not compile, so an
administrator never approves something that fails.

## The shape of a hive

```xml
<q:application id="hive" type="hive">
  <qh:on event="service-crash">
    <qh:offer title="Restart {service}"
              description="{unit} stopped unexpectedly. Run `systemctl restart {service}`."
              action="restart-service" service="{service}" />
    <qh:offer title="Show recent logs for {service}"
              action="run-command" cmd="journalctl" args="-n 50 -u {service}" />
  </qh:on>
  <qh:on event="command-not-found">
    <qh:offer title="Install {package}" action="install-package" package="{package}" />
  </qh:on>

  <qh:allow command="journalctl" args="-n 50 -u *" />   <!-- `*`: any one argument -->
  <qh:allow service="nginx postgresql redis-server" />
  <qh:block service="hive-* systemd-* dbus sshd" />      <!-- a block wins over an allow -->
  <qh:block package="systemd libc6 apt dpkg" />          <!-- never removed -->
  <qh:limit action="install-package" per-minute="5" />
</q:application>
```

The rule on `service-crash` compiles to this, in `rules.toml`, with every
parameter a string that `hive-synapse` types once the fields are filled in:

```toml
[[rules]]
event = "service-crash"

[[rules.offers]]
title = "Restart {service}"
description = "{unit} stopped unexpectedly. Run `systemctl restart {service}`."
action = "restart-service"
service = "{service}"
```

## Attribute types

| Type | What it is |
|---|---|
| `text` | a string; `{field}` placeholders allowed |
| `args` | words separated by spaces, each a placeholder or not |
| `int` | a number, or a `{field}` of a field that is one |
| `bool` | `true` or `false` |
| `words` | one or more names separated by spaces |
| `enum` | one of the values listed |

## The tags

### `qh:on`

What the Hive offers when an event happens: the qh:offers inside, in order. One per event.

Goes inside `<q:application>`.

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event=` | enum: `service-crash`, `log-anomaly`, `port-conflict`, `disk-low`, `memory-pressure`, `command-observed`, `command-not-found` | required |  |

### `qh:offer`

One thing an administrator may approve for the actuator to do. title= and description= are shown on the dashboard; action= names what runs, with the attributes that action takes. Any of them may hold {field}, a field of the event, filled in from the event itself.

Goes inside `<qh:on>`.

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title=` | text | required |  |
| `description=` | text | `` |  |
| `action=` | enum: `run-command`, `start-service`, `stop-service`, `restart-service`, `reload-service`, `enable-service`, `disable-service`, `install-package`, `remove-package`, `update-package-lists`, `upgrade-packages`, `clean-package-cache`, `kill-port-process`, `create-snapshot`, `list-snapshots` | required |  |

Plus the attributes of its `action=`, listed under [the actions](#the-actions).

### `qh:allow`

What the actuator may do at all: its whitelist, which fails closed. Exactly one of command= (with args=: `*` is any one argument; the argument count must match), service=, path=, dataset=, action= (a permission with no list: kill-port-process, open-url, firewall, set-hostname, set-keyboard, set-screen-level, set-network) or delete-snapshot= (the snapshot names the Hive may destroy, a pattern).

Goes inside `<q:application>`.

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command=` | text |  | one program |
| `args=` | args | `` | its arguments, with command= |
| `service=` | words |  | services it may start, stop, restart, reload, enable, disable |
| `path=` | words |  | where files may be created, moved, copied, deleted (patterns) |
| `dataset=` | words |  | ZFS datasets it may snapshot (patterns) |
| `action=` | enum: `kill-port-process`, `open-url`, `firewall`, `set-hostname`, `set-keyboard`, `set-screen-level`, `set-network` |  |  |
| `delete-snapshot=` | text |  | a pattern of snapshot names |

### `qh:block`

What the actuator may never do, whatever is allowed: exactly one of service= (patterns), package= (never removed; patterns) or path= (patterns).

Goes inside `<q:application>`.

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service=` | words |  |  |
| `package=` | words |  |  |
| `path=` | words |  |  |

### `qh:limit`

At most this many of an action a minute, under the actuator's overall limit.

Goes inside `<q:application>`.

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action=` | enum: `run-command`, `create-snapshot`, `restore-snapshot`, `list-snapshots`, `delete-snapshot`, `show-notification`, `open-file`, `open-url`, `install-package`, `remove-package`, `update-package-lists`, `upgrade-packages`, `start-service`, `stop-service`, `restart-service`, `reload-service`, `enable-service`, `disable-service`, `create-directory`, `move-file`, `copy-file`, `delete-file`, `change-permissions`, `kill-port-process`, `add-firewall-rule`, `reboot`, `shutdown`, `suspend`, `clean-package-cache`, `clean-system`, `set-hostname`, `set-keyboard`, `set-screen-level`, `set-network` | required |  |
| `per-minute=` | int | required |  |

## The events

What a `qh:on` can be on: the observations `hive-cortex` passes to `hive-synapse` (`HiveMessage` in `os/crates/hive-common/src/messages.rs`), and the fields an offer may hold as `{field}`.

### `service-crash`

A unit stopped unexpectedly (hive-nerve-journal saw it in the journal). (`ServiceCrash`)

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{unit}` | text | the unit, as systemd names it (nginx.service) |
| `{service}` | text | the service name the actuator uses (nginx); absent when the unit is not a .service, and the offers that need it are left out |
| `{exit_code}` | int | how it exited |

### `log-anomaly`

A unit logs an unusual number of errors. (`LogAnomaly`)

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{unit}` | text | the unit, as systemd names it |
| `{service}` | text | the service name, as in service-crash |

### `port-conflict`

A program could not bind a port another one holds (hive-nerve-network). (`PortConflict`)

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{port}` | int | the port |
| `{requester}` | text | the program that failed to bind |
| `{holder}` | text | the program that holds the port |

### `disk-low`

A filesystem is nearly full. (`DiskSpaceLow`)

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{mount}` | text | the mount point |
| `{percent}` | int | how full, in percent |
| `{free_mb}` | int | megabytes free |

### `memory-pressure`

The system is running low on memory. (`MemoryPressure`)

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{free_mb}` | int | megabytes available |
| `{total_mb}` | int | megabytes in all |

### `command-observed`

A user ran a command the Hive judges dangerous (hive-nerve-process, from the audit log). (`CommandObserved`)

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{cmd}` | text | the command line |
| `{program}` | text | the program |

### `command-not-found`

A user ran a program that is not installed, and a package of that name exists (grove). (`CommandNotFound`)

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `{command}` | text | what the user typed |
| `{package}` | text | the package that would provide it |

## The actions

What a `qh:offer` can name: the `Action` variants `hive-actuator` runs (`os/crates/hive-common/src/actions.rs`), each under the kebab-case of its name, with the attributes it takes.

### `run-command`

Runs a command. It must match a <qh:allow command=> of this file, argument for argument. (`Action::RunCommand`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cmd=` | text | required | the program |
| `args=` | args | `` | its arguments |

### `start-service`

Starts a service (`systemctl start`). (`Action::StartService`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service=` | text | required |  |

### `stop-service`

Stops a service. (`Action::StopService`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service=` | text | required |  |

### `restart-service`

Restarts a service. (`Action::RestartService`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service=` | text | required |  |

### `reload-service`

Reloads a service. (`Action::ReloadService`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service=` | text | required |  |

### `enable-service`

Enables a service at boot, and starts it now unless now=false. (`Action::EnableService`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service=` | text | required |  |
| `now=` | bool | `True` |  |

### `disable-service`

Disables a service at boot, and stops it now unless now=false. (`Action::DisableService`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `service=` | text | required |  |
| `now=` | bool | `True` |  |

### `install-package`

Installs a package through PackageKit, after a safety snapshot. (`Action::InstallPackage`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package=` | text | required |  |

### `remove-package`

Removes a package (never one a <qh:block package=> names), after a safety snapshot; dangerous, so the dashboard asks twice. (`Action::RemovePackage`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package=` | text | required |  |
| `purge=` | bool | `False` | remove its configuration too |

### `update-package-lists`

Refreshes the package lists. (`Action::UpdatePackageLists`)

Takes no attribute.

### `upgrade-packages`

Upgrades packages, after a safety snapshot. (`Action::UpgradePackages`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages=` | words | `` | which; none means all |

### `clean-package-cache`

Cleans the package cache. (`Action::CleanPackageCache`)

Takes no attribute.

### `kill-port-process`

Ends the process holding a port; needs <qh:allow action="kill-port-process"/>. (`Action::KillPortProcess`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `port=` | int | required |  |
| `signal=` | int |  | the signal, 15 when not given |

### `create-snapshot`

Takes a ZFS snapshot of a dataset a <qh:allow dataset=> names. (`Action::CreateSnapshot`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset=` | text | required |  |
| `name=` | text | required |  |
| `recursive=` | bool | `True` |  |

### `list-snapshots`

Lists ZFS snapshots. (`Action::ListSnapshots`)

| Attribute | Type | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset=` | text |  | of one dataset; all when not given |

### What `qh:limit` may name

Every `Action` variant, in kebab-case: `run-command`, `create-snapshot`, `restore-snapshot`, `list-snapshots`, `delete-snapshot`, `show-notification`, `open-file`, `open-url`, `install-package`, `remove-package`, `update-package-lists`, `upgrade-packages`, `start-service`, `stop-service`, `restart-service`, `reload-service`, `enable-service`, `disable-service`, `create-directory`, `move-file`, `copy-file`, `delete-file`, `change-permissions`, `kill-port-process`, `add-firewall-rule`, `reboot`, `shutdown`, `suspend`, `clean-package-cache`, `clean-system`, `set-hostname`, `set-keyboard`, `set-screen-level`, `set-network`.

### What `qh:allow action=` may switch on

`kill-port-process`, `open-url`, `firewall`, `set-hostname`, `set-keyboard`, `set-screen-level`, `set-network`. Off unless the file switches it on.

## What is refused

A compile error names the line. The compiler refuses:

- a tag, an attribute, an event or an action the schema does not list;
- a `{field}` that is not a field of the rule's event, or a text field where a number goes;
- an offer the file's own whitelist would refuse: a command no `qh:allow command=` permits
  (an argument that is a `{field}` needs a `*` in its place), a service no allow permits or a
  block names, a package a block names, a dataset no allow permits, or a permission the file
  does not switch on;
- a `q:` statement, an expression, or text where a tag goes;
- two `qh:on` on one event, a `qh:on` with nothing to offer, a `qh:allow` of two things at once,
  a `qh:limit` given twice or of less than one a minute.

What the compiler cannot check, the daemons do. `hive-synapse` refuses a
`rules.toml` that fails the same checks and uses the rules its build was made
with; an offer whose value is not what its action takes at run time (a port
that is not a number, a unit that is not a service) is left out, never
guessed. `hive-actuator` checks every action against the whitelist, which
fails closed, and rebooting, shutting down and suspending have no switch at
all.

## How it reaches the daemons

`rules.toml` and `whitelist.toml` are installed as `/etc/hive/rules.toml`
and `/etc/hive/whitelist.toml`. The OS's own files are written from
`os/config/hive/hive.q` by `scripts/generate-hive-config.py`, committed as
written and checked in CI, and `hive-synapse` embeds the committed
`rules.toml` as its built-in rules, for a system without the file. The Hive
lab (`os/crates/hive-lab`) plays a tape per rule against the real
`hive-cortex` and `hive-synapse` in a fraction of a second; the VM lab
(`os/scripts/lab/vm`) follows the same rules through the real system.

## The rules Quantum OS ships

`os/config/hive/hive.q`, whole: the five rules and the whitelist the daemons run with.

```xml
<!--
  The Hive's rules, in Quantum: what the Hive offers when something happens,
  and what the actuator may do at all. `quantum run hive.q` (from the
  repository's root: python scripts/generate-hive-config.py) writes
  rules.toml, which hive-synapse loads, and whitelist.toml, which
  hive-actuator loads. Both are committed next to this file and checked
  against it in CI; edit this file, never them.

  A {field} is filled in by hive-synapse from the event itself, never from
  the model's text. An offer this file's own whitelist would refuse does not
  compile. docs/targets/hive.md is the reference.
-->
<q:application id="hive" type="hive">

  <!-- ================================================================ offers -->

  <qh:on event="service-crash">
    <qh:offer title="Restart {service}"
              description="{unit} stopped unexpectedly. Run `systemctl restart {service}`."
              action="restart-service" service="{service}" />
    <qh:offer title="Show recent logs for {service}"
              description="The last 50 journal lines from {service}, to see why it failed."
              action="run-command" cmd="journalctl" args="-n 50 -u {service}" />
  </qh:on>

  <qh:on event="log-anomaly">
    <qh:offer title="Show recent logs for {service}"
              description="The last 50 journal lines from {service}, to see why it failed."
              action="run-command" cmd="journalctl" args="-n 50 -u {service}" />
  </qh:on>

  <qh:on event="disk-low">
    <qh:offer title="Show disk usage"
              description="See how full {mount} and the other mounts are."
              action="run-command" cmd="df" args="-h" />
  </qh:on>

  <qh:on event="command-not-found">
    <qh:offer title="Install {package}"
              description="`{command}` isn't installed; the {package} package provides it."
              action="install-package" package="{package}" />
  </qh:on>

  <qh:on event="port-conflict">
    <qh:offer title="Show listening ports"
              description="See which process is holding port {port}."
              action="run-command" cmd="ss" args="-tlnp" />
  </qh:on>

  <!-- ============================================================= whitelist -->
  <!-- Commands: each matched argument for argument; `*` is any one argument. -->

  <qh:allow command="df" args="-h" />
  <qh:allow command="free" args="-h" />
  <qh:allow command="uptime" />
  <qh:allow command="whoami" />
  <qh:allow command="id" />
  <qh:allow command="uname" args="-a" />
  <qh:allow command="ss" args="-tlnp" />
  <qh:allow command="ip" args="addr" />
  <qh:allow command="ip" args="route" />
  <qh:allow command="systemctl" args="status *" />
  <qh:allow command="systemctl" args="is-active *" />
  <qh:allow command="journalctl" args="-n 50 -u *" />

  <!-- The machine's settings a user asks for through the Ajustes app
       (hive request) and an administrator approves on the screen: its name
       (hostnamectl), its keyboard (us or br), its screen's level, an
       interface's address (netplan; dangerous: Enter twice).
       Two a minute each: a setting is not something to flap. -->
  <qh:allow action="set-hostname" />
  <qh:allow action="set-keyboard" />
  <qh:allow action="set-screen-level" />
  <qh:allow action="set-network" />
  <qh:limit action="set-hostname" per-minute="2" />
  <qh:limit action="set-keyboard" per-minute="2" />
  <qh:limit action="set-screen-level" per-minute="2" />
  <qh:limit action="set-network" per-minute="2" />
  <qh:allow command="zpool" args="status" />
  <qh:allow command="zfs" args="list" />
  <qh:allow command="zfs" args="list -t snapshot" />

  <!-- Services the actuator may start, stop, restart, reload, enable and
       disable; a block wins over an allow, and the Hive and the units that
       keep the machine reachable are never touched. -->
  <qh:allow service="nginx apache2 postgresql mysql mariadb redis-server mongodb docker containerd
                     NetworkManager cups bluetooth" />
  <qh:block service="hive-* systemd-* dbus sshd" />

  <!-- Packages: any valid name may be installed (the per-minute limit below
       bounds it); these are never removed. -->
  <qh:block package="systemd linux-image-* grub-* hive-* zfs-* libc6 apt dpkg" />

  <!-- Files: where they may be created, moved, copied, deleted and have their
       permissions changed, and where never. -->
  <qh:allow path="/home/* /tmp/* /var/tmp/*" />
  <qh:block path="/home/*/.ssh/* /home/*/.gnupg/* /etc/* /usr/* /bin/* /sbin/* /lib/* /boot/* /root/*" />

  <!-- ZFS: the datasets it may snapshot, and the snapshots it may destroy
       (only the Hive's own). -->
  <qh:allow dataset="rpool/ROOT/* rpool/home/*" />
  <qh:allow delete-snapshot="hive-*" />

  <!-- Permissions with no list behind them. Rebooting, shutting down and
       suspending have no switch: never. -->
  <qh:allow action="kill-port-process" />
  <qh:allow action="open-url" />

  <!-- At most this many a minute, under the actuator's overall limit. -->
  <qh:limit action="kill-port-process" per-minute="10" />
  <qh:limit action="install-package" per-minute="5" />
  <qh:limit action="remove-package" per-minute="3" />
  <qh:limit action="create-directory" per-minute="20" />
  <qh:limit action="move-file" per-minute="20" />
  <qh:limit action="copy-file" per-minute="20" />
  <qh:limit action="delete-file" per-minute="20" />
  <qh:limit action="change-permissions" per-minute="20" />
  <qh:limit action="create-snapshot" per-minute="10" />
  <qh:limit action="restore-snapshot" per-minute="10" />
  <qh:limit action="delete-snapshot" per-minute="10" />

</q:application>
```
